title: Learned MRI analysis distinguishes postanoxic coma from healthy controls in a small cohort
summary: A three-dimensional convolutional network distinguished 29 postanoxic-coma patients from 34 healthy volunteers using structural and functional MRI measurements. Posterior-cingulate functional connectivity provided the strongest reported internal discrimination, outperforming the tested structural inputs. The result is a small clinical imaging feasibility study, without independently validated prediction of recovery or demonstrated bedside benefit.
ai_technology: Custom three-dimensional convolutional neural network for multimodal brain MRI classification
organization: Toulouse III Paul Sabatier University; Inserm; CNRS; Toulouse University Hospital

evidence.tested: A prospectively collected single-center cohort included 29 postanoxic-coma patients and 34 healthy volunteers. Separate structural and functional MRI inputs were evaluated with a custom 3D CNN using ten-times repeated tenfold cross-validation. Input intensity normalization used training-set values. Posterior-cingulate functional-connectivity inputs achieved reported mean accuracy 0.96, versus 0.82 for T1 structural input.
evidence.unknown: Small groups, a healthy-control contrast, one scanner/center and repeated internal cross-validation limit clinical specificity and generalization. Prospective collection is not an external locked-model evaluation. Convolutional activation maps were derived from correctly classified training samples and do not establish causal consciousness mechanisms. Post-hoc favorable outcomes among a few misclassified patients are not independent recovery prediction. No clinical deployment, prognosis-guided intervention or outcome benefit was demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: The trained 3D CNN learned spatial features from patient and control MRI volumes, enabling the represented clinical-status discrimination and comparison of the informative content of different MRI inputs.

source_review.scope: Read actual primary patient/control and clinical reference selection, imaging input, 3D CNN architecture/training/normalization/cross-validation Methods, modality-comparison Results and interpretive limitations. Post-hoc recovery hints and training activation maps are not admitted as validated prognosis or causal mechanisms.
